setup: (fset 'my-when (if (fboundp 'defmacro) (cons 'macro (lambda (c b) (list 'if c b))) (macro (c b) (list 'if c b))))
note: 10B: a transformer applied through `macroexpand-1` is arity-checked exactly as a direct call is, and the count is the macro call's, not `macroexpand-1`'s. Shaped like arity-lambda-too-few-nargs and for the same reason: the symbol and NARGS are pulled out in Lisp so that neither side's rendering of the FUNCTION element -- Emacs' `#[(a) ((not a)) nil]` against fe's macro name -- takes part (phase7-arity-condition-rendering records that). The setup is dialect-neutral by construction: Emacs stores a macro as a `(macro . FUNCTION)` cons in the function cell and fe has a distinct macro object, so each transformer is installed through whichever spelling the running dialect has, selected by `(fboundp 'defmacro)` -- t in Emacs, nil in standalone fe. Nothing else about the case differs between the sides. The transformers deliberately expand to forms both dialects spell identically (`if`, `+`, `not`): fe's implicit body is `do` where Emacs' is `progn`, and that is not what these cases are about. (fe's printer used to be the other half of this note: it wrote `(quote x)` out where Emacs abbreviates it to `'x`. Sub-plan 11C closed that divergence -- see writer-quote-forms -- so both sides abbreviate now, and the transformers above would be safe either way.)
